sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Context**: Post-WWI, the price of silver skyrocketed, making the existing **15 rupees = 1 pound sterling** ratio unsustainable.
• **Objective**: To stabilize the Indian exchange rate and determine the relationship between the Rupee and the Gold Sovereign.
• **Core Recommendation**: The committee recommended fixing the exchange rate at **2 shillings per rupee** (10 rupees = 1 pound sterling).
• **Key Metric**: The shift from a silver-based currency to a gold-linked exchange standard to protect British commercial interests.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Led to massive economic distress in India
Maintenance of sterling reserves in London
Criticized by Indian nationalists as 'Drain of Wealth'

items.definition: A system where the local currency is pegged to a foreign currency (Sterling) which is itself convertible to gold, rather than the local currency being directly convertible to gold.
A mechanism used by the British to sell sterling in India to maintain the high exchange rate, which effectively drained India's gold reserves.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Currency Stabilization**: Attempt to align Indian currency with the post-war British Sterling.
• **Monetary Centralization**: Strengthening the role of the Secretary of State for India in managing currency reserves.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Economic Impact**: The high exchange rate made Indian exports expensive and imports cheap, causing a trade deficit.
• **Nationalist Backlash**: Indian leaders like Purshottamdas Thakurdas opposed the report, leading to the later Hilton Young Commission.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'B-S-2' (Babington-Smith = 2 shillings).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Babington Smith Commission recommended the Rupee be valued at 2 shillings.

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the Babington Smith Commission (1919) with the Hilton Young Commission (1926). Remember: Babington Smith = 2 shillings; Hilton Young = Establishment of RBI.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Monetary Imperialism' to describe how the commission prioritized British trade stability over Indian economic health.

keyTakeaways: The Babington Smith Commission recommended a 2-shilling exchange rate.
It failed to stabilize the economy and led to a massive drain of gold reserves.
Its failure necessitated the subsequent Hilton Young Commission (1926).
